title: Hot-run telemetry scratchpad: segmented E2E trace notes
content:
Context:
This is a fast-moving scratchpad capturing a cluster of long tail traces from a weekend hot-run. Goal: capture raw observations, quick stage-level breakdowns (tokenize -> preprocess -> kv-lookup -> kernel-> emit -> egress), surface hypotheses for p95/p99 regressions, and propose repro experiment steps. Not intended as the final postmortem — more of a field notebook for next-day pairing.

Summary observations (high level):
- Baseline route: chat-completions with moderate seqlen (prompt ~512 tokens, gen target ~256).
- Observed p50 ~ 120ms, p95 ~ 420ms, p99 ~ 1.6s for this route during the hot run window (2025-02-09 02:30-05:10 UTC).
- Tail traces cluster into two phenotypes: (A) long kernel stalls (GPU compute dominated) and (B) sporadic stall while waiting on KV cache misses + async batch handoffs. Roughly 60% of p99 traces are phenotype B.

Per-stage sampled breakdown (representative aggregated numbers from 1k sampled end-to-end traces):
- Tokenize: p50 3ms, p95 5ms, p99 12ms
- Preprocess (routing + auth checks): p50 6ms, p95 12ms, p99 40ms
- KV-cache lookup: p50 5ms, p95 18ms, p99 420ms (heavy tail due to remote shard retries)
- Batcher wait (time spent queued waiting for batch): p50 4ms, p95 30ms, p99 520ms
- Kernel compute (model forward + attention): p50 75ms, p95 165ms, p99 400ms
- Emit/serialization: p50 2ms, p95 6ms, p99 18ms
- Egress (network + flush): p50 25ms, p95 80ms, p99 200ms

Notes on KV and batching interaction:
- Many traces show KV-cache lookup crossing into remote RPCs when per-shard TTL expired; these remote hits add variable 200-500ms latency and occasional retries due to flaky link. See traces: trace ids [t-20250209-1, t-20250209-7, t-20250209-13] in tracestore.
- When KV misses occur, async-batcher handoff sometimes stalls: our batcher has a time-window fallback (max-wait 25ms) but in practice we observed handoff loops prompting longer waits because previous batch commit was delayed by kernel spikes.

Hypotheses (rank-ordered):
1) KV cache TTL misalignment across replicas: stale TTLs cause more RPCs than expected => elevated p95/p99.
2) Bursty kernel scheduling (GPU preemption + multi-tenant noise) creates compute spikes that ripple back to batcher, increasing queue time.
3) RPC retry/backoff knob too conservative for transient link errors, magnifying tail.
4) Egress path congestion for the AZ during window (packet drops leading to retransmits).

Immediate repro experiments to run (fast, short):
- Controlled replay: take 300 p99-ish requests (sanitized) and replay against a single dedicated dev node with local KV golden set (no remote RPC). Compare distribution. Linear: RD-4121.
- Isolate kernel: run same request set on dedicated instance with kernel telemetry enabled (detailed CUDA kernel timelines) and compare compute tail to prod.
- Force cache warm: pre-populate per-shard KV for a cohort and replay to measure delta.

Quick commands / where to find assets:
- Tracestore queries: SELECT * FROM traces WHERE trace_id IN (t-20250209-1,t-20250209-7,t-20250209-13) — saved view: /observability/saved/hotrun-feb9
- Replayer: tools/replayer --tracefile traces/hotrun-feb9-sample.ndjson --target dev-node-12 --kv-mode local
- Kernel timeline viewer: https://gpu-debugger.internal/trace/t-20250209-1

Immediate mitigation options (quick wins):
- Lower KV RPC retry attempts from 3 -> 1 for cache lookup path (risk: transient misses may surface more often; communicate with CS).
- Short-term increase max-batcher parallelism to reduce queuing when kernel jitter observed (watch e2e latency).
- Pin small cohort to dedicated GPU hosts in Canary to see if p99 improves (rollout plan with canary fraction 1%).

Longer-term actions:
- TTL alignment audit across cache shards + stronger observability on cache hit/miss per-request. (Owner: Priya Nair)
- Kernel fairness scheduling investigation (SRE + infra) to reduce preemption noise (Owner: Miguel Ortega).
- Backoff policy review for RPC layer and add circuit-breaker metrics (Owner: Samir Patel).

Open questions / TODOs:
- How many distinct customers impacted? Need to map request coalescing (user vs system). (TODO: join CS export for feb9)
- Are there correlated infra events in cloud provider logs? (TODO: ask infra for network metrics for the AZ window)
- Can we collect a lightweight KV-provenance header on requests to quickly attribute misses? (Engineering spike).

Next steps (this week):
- Claire & Miguel: run controlled replay & collect kernel timelines (target: 2025-03-05)
short_summary: Working notes capturing multi-phenotype p95/p99 tail from a weekend hot run; KV misses + batcher interaction identified as dominant contributor to long tails. Contains per-stage sample breakdowns, hypotheses, and quick repro/mitigation steps.
